title: Grade 5 Math — Thu, Jun 12
description: Simple Interest — Day 4 of 5: Real-life applications
subject: mathematics

questions.question: Sita keeps ₹8000 in a savings account at 6% per year for 4 years. What is her total SI?
Ramesh needs to repay ₹5500 after 1 year on a ₹5000 loan. What was the rate of interest?
A shopkeeper lends ₹10000 at 9% per year. He earns ₹2700 as interest. For how many years was the money lent?
Meena borrowed ₹4500 at 8% per year for 2 years. How much does she pay back in total?
Banks give more interest for ___ time periods.
questions.explanation: Since SI increases with time (T), longer deposits earn more interest.

questions.question: Vijay invested ₹20000 at 7.5% per year for 2 years. What is the interest earned?
If the principal is ₹0, what is the simple interest (any rate, any time)?
questions.explanation: SI = (0 × R × T) ÷ 100 = ₹0. No principal means no interest.

questions.question: Ranjit borrowed money and paid ₹450 as interest at 9% per year for 2 years. What was the principal?
P = ₹6000 at 5% for T years gives SI = ₹900. What is T?
A person gets ₹400 as interest at 4% for 2 years. What was the principal?
Which is better for the borrower — 6% for 2 years or 4% for 3 years (same P)?
questions.explanation: For P=₹100: 6%×2=12; 4%×3=12. They're equal! But for a general case, check both.

questions.question: Lata borrowed ₹7000 at 6% per year. After how many years will the SI be ₹2100?
At what rate per year will ₹1500 become ₹1800 in 4 years?
A post office gives 8% simple interest per year. If Mohan deposits ₹2500, after 2 years the amount is ___.
The interest on ₹3600 for 2 years is ₹576. The rate of interest is ___.
